name: BNSF Railway
tagline: Agentic ops for a 32,500-mile freight network — safer trains, sharper service, faster customer resolution.
overview: BNSF moves agricultural, industrial, energy, automotive, and intermodal freight across one of North America’s largest rail networks. Agentic AI can compress service exception handling, demurrage disputes, claims assembly, and customer pricing/support loops while keeping safety-critical and regulatory actions under human control.
painPoints: Service exceptions and advisories require stitching network, weather, and customer commitments across siloed systems
Demurrage, storage, and cargo claims consume analyst time assembling evidence from multiple portals
Shippers struggle to get rates, ETAs, and issue resolution without multi-touch customer assistance
strategicImpact: Faster exception-to-recovery cycle time across carload and intermodal
Lower demurrage dispute and claims handling cost per case
Higher first-contact resolution in customer and driver/dispatcher support

singleAgents.name: Service Advisory Synthesizer
singleAgents.role: Turns network events into customer-ready service impact briefs
singleAgents.trigger: New service advisory, facility update, or network disruption signal
singleAgents.output: Impacted lanes/commodities list + draft customer notification + recommended mitigation options
singleAgents.roi: 1–3 hours saved per major advisory; fewer reactive call-center spikes

singleAgents.name: Demurrage Dispute Packager
singleAgents.role: Assembles demurrage/storage timelines and draft dispute responses
singleAgents.trigger: Customer disputes demurrage/storage charges or invoice exception created
singleAgents.output: Chronology packet, rule citations, and recommended uphold/adjust disposition
singleAgents.roi: 30–60 min saved per dispute; more consistent tariff application

singleAgents.name: Cargo Claim Dossier Agent
singleAgents.role: Builds cargo loss and damage claim evidence packages
singleAgents.trigger: Claim filed via customer tools or customer assistance
singleAgents.output: Submission-ready claim dossier with liability hypothesis and missing-evidence checklist
singleAgents.roi: 2–4 hours saved per complex claim; faster time-to-decision

singleAgents.name: Ship-With-BNSF Concierge
singleAgents.role: Guides new and existing shippers through rate, routing, and tracking questions
singleAgents.trigger: Customer portal chat/ticket or 'new to rail' inquiry
singleAgents.output: Answer with cited tools, next-step checklist, or precise handoff to pricing/sales
singleAgents.roi: 20–35% deflection of repetitive customer assistance contacts

multiAgent.name: Network Service Recovery Cell
multiAgent.description: A supervisor-led multi-agent team that owns disruption-to-recovery for affected shipments — from perception through customer communication — without changing safety-critical train control.

supervisor.name: Service Recovery Supervisor
supervisor.responsibilities: Owns blast radius assessment for a disruption, sequences specialist work, decides when to escalate to human network/service managers, and prevents conflicting customer commitments.
supervisor.routingLogic: Network/asset issues → Movement Truth Agent; capacity/recrew/re-route options → Replan Agent; customer SLA impact → Customer Impact Agent; commercial/accessorial risk → Commercial Guard Agent.

subAgents.name: Movement Truth Agent
responsibilities: Merge car location, interchange, and facility events
Flag data gaps or conflicting scans
subAgents.contextHandoff: Trusted movement state and ETA confidence to Supervisor

subAgents.name: Replan Agent
responsibilities: Propose alternate routings or hold/release strategies
Estimate recovery time vs. cost tradeoffs
subAgents.contextHandoff: Ranked recovery options with constraints for Supervisor decision

subAgents.name: Customer Impact Agent
responsibilities: Map affected BOs/shipments to customers and commodities
Draft service notifications aligned to advisory templates
Offer self-serve tracking next steps in the customer portal
subAgents.contextHandoff: Segmented notification drafts and escalation list

subAgents.name: Commercial Guard Agent
responsibilities: Flag promises that conflict with tariff or contract terms
subAgents.contextHandoff: Commercial risk memo before external commitments lock

multiAgent.conflictResolution: Safety and operating rules always override service speed. No customer ETA or commercial concession is sent without human service-desk approval when confidence is low or $ exposure exceeds threshold. Conflicting movement data pauses replan until Movement Truth Agent reconciles or a human dispatcher confirms. Train control / PTC systems remain out of agent write-scope.

workflow.label: Input
workflow.description: Ingest disruption signal (weather, facility outage, congestion, mechanical) plus affected cars/trains, customer commitments, and open advisories from network and customer systems.

workflow.label: Reason
workflow.description: Service Recovery Supervisor builds a blast-radius hypothesis, prioritizes premium/intermodal/agriculture windows, and selects which specialist agents to run.

workflow.label: Tool Execution
workflow.description: Agents fuse movement events, score recovery options, draft customer notifications, and estimate demurrage/commercial exposure using approved BNSF tools and read APIs.

workflow.label: Human-in-the-Loop
workflow.description: Network/service managers approve recovery strategy and external messaging; commercial teams approve any tariff exceptions or goodwill; safety-critical actions never auto-execute.

workflow.label: Output
workflow.description: Customers receive accurate advisories via notification channels; internal ops board updates; lessons are written back to the service playbook knowledge base.

apis: BNSF Customer Portal (tracking, billing, shipping tools)
Supplier Portal (invoices, POs) for adjacent procurement ops
vectorDbs: Shipping instructions checklists and commodity guides (ag, intermodal, hazmat)
Historical service advisories and recovery playbooks
Safety rule excerpts appropriate for non-control advisory use
legacySystems: EDI gateways (e.g., waybill, car location messages)
security: Strict separation from Positive Train Control and safety-critical control systems
Customer data minimization and portal-scoped auth
Hazmat and security information need-to-know controls
Full audit trail for notifications, disputes, and claim dispositions
Maker-checker for commercial concessions and external advisories
